column2: The portico of my eye's outlook is your nest / show generosity and come down, for the house is your house
With the grace of mole and down you stole the heart from the knowers / wondrous subtleties lie under your snare and grain
May your heart be glad in union with the rose, O nightingale of dawn / for in the meadow all is your lover's song
Refer the cure of our heart's weakness to the lip / for this ruby cordial is in your treasury
In body I fall short of the fortune of attending you / but the essence of the soul is the dust of your threshold
I am not one who gives the coin of the heart to every saucy one / the treasury's door is under your seal and your mark
What a doll you are yourself, O sweet-working royal rider / that an unbroken horse like the sky is tame to your whip
What room for me, when the juggling sky slips / on these tricks that are in your bag of pretexts
Now the sky brings the song of your assembly to dance / for the poetry of sweet-spoken Hafez is your melody
Go about your business, O preacher, what is this outcry? / my heart fell from the road; what has befallen you?
In his waist, which God created from nothing / is a subtlety that no created being has unravelled
Until his lip brings me to my desire, like a reed-flute / the advice of the whole world is wind in my ear
The beggar of your street has no need of the eight paradises / the captive of your love is free of both worlds
Though the drunkenness of love has ruined me, yet / the foundation of my being is made prosperous by that ruin
O heart, do not lament the injustice and cruelty of the beloved, for the beloved / made this your portion, and this is justice from that
Go, do not recite fables and do not breathe spells, Hafez / for of this fable and spell I remember much
Since the tip of your hair fell into the hand of the breeze / the love-crazed heart has fallen in two from grief
Your sorcerer's eye is itself the very script of magic / but this is so, that this copy has turned out sick
Do you know what that black mole is in the curl of your hair? / a dot of ink that has fallen into the loop of a jim
Your musky hair in the paradise-garden of the cheek / what is it? a peacock that has fallen into the garden of bliss
My heart in longing for your face, O companion of the soul / is the dust of a road that has fallen into the hand of the breeze
Like dust this earthly body cannot rise / from the head of your street, because it has fallen so heavily
The shadow of your stature on my frame, O you of Jesus's breath / is the reflection of a spirit fallen on decayed bone
He who, from memory of your lip, had no station but the Kaaba / I saw at the tavern's door, fallen there to stay
Lost Hafez has, with your grief, O dear friend / a union that fell to him in the ancient covenant
